sources.title: Generate OpenAPI documents — ASP.NET Core .NET 10
sources.finding: Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi supports OpenAPI 3.1 document generation on .NET 10, including runtime and build-time generation; the P1 scope uses only the first-party executable-contract baseline.

sources.title: What is new in ASP.NET Core in .NET 10 — OpenAPI 3.1 support
sources.finding: ASP.NET Core .NET 10 generates OpenAPI 3.1 documents and documents the associated OpenAPI.NET 2.0 compatibility considerations; no OpenAPI 3.2 claim is made for this .NET 10 scope.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.1.2
sources.finding: OpenAPI 3.1 defines the HTTP API description contract and treats patch releases within the 3.1 feature set as compatible for supporting tooling.

decision: Use the .NET 10 first-party OpenAPI pipeline as the executable OpenAPI 3.1 baseline required by ADR-0011. Publish only a technical contract artifact; defer Product operations, schemas, SDK generation, authentication, interactive UI, and public exposure to their owning governed work items.
limitations: This evidence verifies current tool and standards compatibility only; it does not authorize a Product API, endpoint taxonomy, public documentation site, SDK release, or external publication.
OpenAPI 3.2 remains a forward target and may become normative only through the approved runtime/tooling upgrade trigger in ADR-0011.
Refresh these primary sources before changing the OpenAPI generator, published-contract behavior, or external API scope.
